question_text: The function $f$ can be written in the form $f(x) = a(x - p)(x - q)$ where $p > q$.

subparts.stem: Write down the values of $p$ and $q$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Identifying $x$-intercepts from the graph as $-1$ and $5$

subparts.solution: $y = f(x) = a(x - p)(x - q)$ has $x$-intercepts $-1$ and $5$. $\therefore p = 5$ and $q = -1$ (or $p > q$).

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In factored form $f(x) = a(x - p)(x - q)$, $p$ and $q$ represent the $x$-intercepts of the quadratic function.
step_by_step: From the sketch, read the $x$-intercepts where $y = 0$, which are $x = -1$ and $x = 5$.
Match with the formula $a(x - p)(x - q)$. Since $p > q$, assign $p = 5$ and $q = -1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mixing up the signs of the roots inside the factors, e.g., writing $x - (-1) = x - 1$.

subparts.solution: From a, $f(x) = a(x - 5)(x + 1)$. From the graph, $f(0) = -20$. $\therefore -20 = a(-5)(1) \implies -20 = -5a \implies a = 4$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The leading coefficient $a$ can be determined by substituting the coordinates of any known point on the graph into the factored form.
step_by_step: Write the function with known roots: $f(x) = a(x - 5)(x + 1)$.

subparts.stem: Write down the equation of the axis of symmetry.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using the midpoint formula on the $x$-intercepts
Finding equation of the axis of symmetry $x = 2$

subparts.solution: The axis of symmetry is midway between the $x$-intercepts. $\therefore$ the axis of symmetry is $x = \frac{-1 + 5}{2} = 2$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The axis of symmetry of a parabola passes through the midpoint of the two $x$-intercepts: $x = \frac{p + q}{2}$.
step_by_step: State the equation of the vertical line: $x = 2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Giving just the number $2$ instead of the equation of the line $x = 2$.
